chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man passes through intending to go to Yemen or other cities, and his route is through Mecca, so he catches up with the people as they are setting out for Hajj, and he sets out with them to the shrines. Would that suffice him as the Hajj of Islam? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Does a traveler passing through Mecca fulfill their Hajj obligation by joining the pilgrims?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a traveler passing through Mecca who joins the pilgrims in performing the rites at the shrines fulfills their obligation of Hajj al-Islam, even without prior intention. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of Hajj for those who are not originally pilgrims but participate in the rituals, emphasizing the importance of the actual performance of rites over strict initial intent. The hadith underscores the principle that joining the communal act of worship in the sacred precincts is sufficient for discharging the religious duty.
